_schema_notes.purpose: Union label dating rules. Union existence dates are historical record (high confidence). Specific label design era dates are approximations based on documented design changes and may need refinement.
_schema_notes.type_hard_bound: Garment cannot exist outside these dates.
_schema_notes.type_soft_anchor: Strong probability toward this range; exceptions possible.
_schema_notes.confidence: high = historical fact or very well documented, medium = generally accepted but ±2-3 years possible, low = rough estimate needing verification

existence_bound.notes: ILGWU merged into UNITE in February 1995. Any garment bearing an ILGWU label predates 1995. One of the most common union labels on American vintage women's clothing.

pre_1936_no_scallop.notes: Very early ILGWU labels without the scalloped circle design. Extremely rare.

AFL_only.notes: AFL merged with CIO in December 1955 to form AFL-CIO. Labels reading 'AFL' without 'CIO' predate the merger. Hard ceiling of 1955.

1936_CIO.notes: During 1936-1940 a faction of ILGWU was affiliated with CIO following a union split. Labels reading 'ILGWU CIO' indicate this short window.

1955_1963_scallop_needle.notes: Design features large scalloped circle surrounding a union logo in front of needle and thread, 'UNION LABEL' above, AFL-CIO below. Tightly brackets garment to 1955-1963.

1963_1974_dark_circle.notes: Large scalloped circle with dark inner circle, 'UNION MADE' at top, 'ILGWU' in center, 'AFL-CIO' at bottom. If a small circled-R trademark symbol appears below the scallop, garment is post April 21, 1964.

1964_R_trademark.notes: Small circled-R below scalloped circle — trademark registered April 21, 1964. Narrows to 1964-1974.

1974_1995_red_white_blue.notes: Same scalloped/dark-circle design as 1963-1974 but in red, white, and blue. The most commonly seen ILGWU label. This is the 'patriotic' era label that most collectors recognize.

AFL_CIO_generic.notes: AFL-CIO affiliation present but sub-design unclear. Use when specific design era is not identifiable.

look_for_the_union_label_campaign.notes: The 'Look for the Union Label' advertising campaign launched 1975. Labels or hang tags explicitly referencing this campaign postdate 1975.

existence_bound.notes: ACWA merged with the Textile Workers Union of America in 1976 to form ACTWU. Label is conclusive proof of pre-1976 production.

ACTWU.full_name: Amalgamated Clothing and Textile Workers Union

existence_bound.notes: Formed from merger of ACWA and TWU in 1976. Merged into UNITE in 1995. Tight 19-year window.
Merged with ACWA in 1976. Less common on finished garments than ILGWU/ACWA.

AFL_CIO.notes: AFL-CIO affiliation brackets this label to 1956-1976.

UNITE.full_name: Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees

existence_bound.notes: Formed from ILGWU + ACTWU merger in 1995. Merged with HERE in 2004 to form UNITE HERE. Rarely seen on garments — domestic union production was declining sharply during this window.
Formed in 2004. Extremely rare on garment labels given near-total offshore shift by this point. Presence would be notable and likely indicates a specialty or boutique domestic producer.

Technically still exists but became largely inactive after losing jurisdiction to ACWA in the mid-20th century. UGWA labels on garments are predominantly pre-1950. Seeing this label is a strong early-to-mid 20th century signal.

BRAC.full_name: Brotherhood of Railway, Airline and Steamship Clerks
BRAC.notes: Occasionally appears on garments made for rail/transport workers. Limited dating utility without sub-design research. Flag for manual review.

existence_bound.notes: BRAC merged into TCU in 1988. Appearance on clothing labels is rare and context-specific.
